examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Law that Conjunction Absorbs Disjunction
examples.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $X?$

- $X \land (Y \lor X)$

- $(X \lor Y) \land Y$

- $(X \lor Y) \land X$
examples.worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
X \land (X \lor Y) \equiv X.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is logically equivalent to $X.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}X∧(Y∨X) & ≡X∧(X∨Y) \\  & ≡X.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is *not* logically equivalent to $X.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(Y∨X)∧Y & ≡Y∧(Y∨X) \\  & ≡Y≢X.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $X.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(X∨Y)∧X & ≡X∧(X∨Y) \\  & ≡X.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
